whatItIs.text: A bright, clean-tasting herb from the carrot family — flat-leaf (stronger flavour, chefs' choice) and curly (the classic garnish).

historyNote.text: Parsley is native to Greece, the Balkans, Algeria, and Morocco, and was cultivated by the 3rd century BC; its name descends from Greek petroselinon, 'rock-celery', and it reached England in 1548.

howToChoose.text: Choose perky, deep-green bunches with no slimy or yellowed stems; flat-leaf for cooking and salads, curly where texture matters.

storage.text: Stand in a jar of water, loosely bagged, in the fridge.

useItUp.text: Wilted parsley still works chopped into gremolata, tabbouleh, or chimichurri, or dried low and slow in the oven for later.

substitutions.note: delicate anise note; add at the very end
same freshness family; slightly bitter edge
